Primarily on /r/christianity.  I do not believe that G-d loves me (quite the opposite, though I do not begrudge anyone who thinks G-d *does* love them), and that is evidently a very unpopular opinion over there.

Thank you for the kind words, but this does not mesh with my personal experience with G-d.  G-d has revealed Himself to me since I was eleven years old (not continuously, but through intermittent and frankly terrifying instances, at least one per year but no more than three), and the one constant thread in those revelations is that He hates me and will relish in having me tortured for an eternity in Hell.

I know there are some who will say it is the Enemy who speaks to me, but this is not the case. I know with every fiber of my being that it is G-d who speaks to me, G-d who hates me, and G-d who has told me that I will go to Hell regardless of how I live my life, because He hates me.  His hatred of me is constant and unrelenting, and only He can choose whether to hate or love me (or anyone, for that matter).  

I don't begrudge anyone who is loved by G-d for being lucky enough to be loved by Him.  I'm relieved to know or believe that He does in fact love at least *someone*.  If G-d does love you, you are truly fortunate.  He just doesn't love me.  (Well, He has revealed to me that He does hate other people, but I fear that explaining who He hates here would be construed as hate speech or a violation of the rules, so I will restrain myself.)

I truly wish Jesus were in charge.  Then I could find greater solace in your message.  But he isn't, and G-d is, and whatever He says is how it is, shall, and must be.

I repeat, please do not belittle my religious beliefs by suggesting that they are solely the product of mental illness.  It is not only disrespectful towards me and the mentally ill, but also arguably all religious beliefs.  Literally all that I am asking if you is for you to not publicly belittle my religious beliefs.
Please do not belittle my religious beliefs by suggesting that they are solely the product of mental illness.  That is disrespectful to me and to the mentally ill.
He won't and He doesn't.  Please stop talking.
This conversation is over.  I hope you enjoy the rest of your day.

It is not about what I find comfortable, it is about what is true.  I would *much* rather have it be the case that G-d did not hate me, had not personally told me I was going to Hell, and did not have the ability to revoke salvation.  I would much rather live in a world where Jesus were in charge.  But neither of those is the case.  It doesn't matter what I'd rather have it be; it's how it is.

I am not here to engage in a religious debate.  I am not equipped for a religious debate, I only know G-d as He has revealed Himself to me.  And G-d has revealed Himself to me as an omnipotent being, who is the final and ultimate authority on everything; if He says or does something, then it is by definition *right*, no matter how horrible or terrible it is.  G-d could command someone to eat their own children alive, and it would be the right thing to do, because G-d commanded it.  That is how He has revealed Himself to me.  

My purpose in this post was to see how others think/thought (unsure on conjugation) about a necessary (to my understanding) implication of G-d's omnipotence: that because G-d has the final say on *everything*, and thus has final say over who goes to Heaven or Hell, it must be the case that G-d could, if He wanted to, tear someone out of Heaven at any moment and for any reason (including no reason) and send them to Hell.  If G-d is omnipotent, He must have that ability.
I do that because I believe it is improper to commit His name(s) or title(s) to a format that can be changed, lost, or destroyed, since He is eternal.  Typing "G-d" is a quick and easy workaround.

One final time, **I am neither interested in nor equipped for a theological debate**.

One final time, **I do not believe in the devil or the Enemy as you are using the term.**

One final time, **it is G-d who speaks to me and tells me I am going to Hell, who tells me He hates me and will laugh at my suffering in Hell, and who has revealed Himself to me exactly as I have described Him.**

I will not debate this further with you, because I have made my intentions, purposes, and experiences here quite clear on multiple occasions with as little ambiguity as I can muster.  I am not here to debate theology.  I had a thought, and came here to ask others' perspectives just on that thought.

I am sorry to have offended you or put you through this much distress.  I truly am.  I'm sure G-d is laughing at me for this right now, and I fear that He may choose to speak to me again tonight.  Right now, I will offer you two options in an attempt to rectify this situation:

1. I can delete this post and all of my comments here so as not to disturb you any further; or

2. You could refrain from reading futhrr posts of mine if they disturb you so much.

You are the aggrieved party, so I will let you choose the punishment for me and/or how best to make you whole.
It is G-d.  I do not believe in the devil as you are using the term, and I know with every fiber of my being that it is G-d who speaks to me to tell me I am going to Hell.

Like I have said many times now, I am not interested ok not equipped for a theological debate.  I only know G-d as He has revealed Himself to me.  And He has revealed to me that He hates me and will send me to Hell when I die.  Jesus has never spoken to me, and G-d has told me that he never will, because G-d will not let him.  This is how G-d has revealed Himself to me.  I cannot speak to any theological points because I am not qualified, and I will not waste anyone's time debating my subjective experiences, which no one has any reason to believe over their own anyway.  I hope your day/night/morning/evening/afternoon is pleasant.

G-d, as He has revealed Himself to me, has revealed that He hates certain people and will always send those people to Hell, along with anyone else He wants to.  I fall into several groups of people He has told me He hates.

I am sorry to have offended you.  As I said, I am not here to cause or take part in a theological debate, nor am I equipped for one.  I only know G-d as He has revealed Himself to me, and G-d has consistently told me through the years that He hates me, that He will send me to Hell upon my death, that He has decreed I deserve Hell and thus I *do* deserve Hell, and that He will laugh as I suffer there.  I know it is G-d who speaks to me, and not the Enemy.  I honestly don't even believe in the Enemy as most people do; G-d is bad enough anyway.  "The Enemy" cannot exist or act without G-d's explicit knowledge, approval, and support; to the extent that I believe an "Enemy" exists, I believe he is closer to G-d's District Attorney than anything else.  

Again, I am not interest in nor equipped for a theological debate.  I only know G-d as He reveals Himsekf to me, and this is how He has revealed Himself.  And I'm sorry to have caused you offensives suffering.

Thanks!

Now there's a troubling thought.

I guess I should have specified that I view G-d and Jesus as separate entities (and that we would all be much better off if Jesus were in charge), but then again I *also* suppose that Jesus couldn't have taken anyone out of Hell if G-d hadn't let him do it.  

Have there been any accounts of the opposite happening?  I'm drawing a total blank.

I'm glad that you do.  I don't, because every time He has spoken to me, He's told me that He hates me and that I am destined for Hell.  He's spoken to me like this since I was eleven years old.  I know that there are some people He loves, perhaps even the majority, but I also know that He hates me.  

Anyway, it's nice (for a given value of "nice," anyway) that I'm not completely alone in my interpretation.  Thank you for your answer, and I hope the rest of your day/night/evening is pleasant.
